subject.title: fix: forward response-frame meta to clients

question: Should OpenClaw accept optional `res.meta` as an additive v4 response-envelope field after this PR is rebased, or require a versioned/negotiated protocol path for strict clients?
rationale: The patch fixes a real metadata drop and official clients appear tolerant or updated, but the public response envelope is strict in the protocol schema and only maintainers can accept that same-version compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Accept after rebase
options.body: Resolve the conflicts, keep `meta` optional/defaulted, and merge under the additive-protocol policy with documented strict-client tolerance.

options.title: Require versioning
options.body: Ask for a protocol-version or negotiation path if maintainers do not want same-version top-level response fields to reach strict external validators.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Leave the PR open but blocked until a gateway/protocol owner decides the response-envelope compatibility policy.

recommendation.title: Accept after rebase
recommendation.body: Resolve the conflicts, keep `meta` optional/defaulted, and merge under the additive-protocol policy with documented strict-client tolerance.

likelyOwner.reason: He is tied both to the shared `RespondFn` type surface and to recent merged gateway/protocol changes, making him the best available routing owner for the compatibility decision.
